title: Acombamack
summary: Acombamack is a Long Island Algonquian placename associated with the neck of land where Bellport is now located in Brookhaven. The place is described in relation to Great South Bay and the land between Daytons Brook and Overtons Brook, with Owenamchock treated as a related boundary and fishing-place form.
address_label: General Bellport / Great South Bay area, Brookhaven, NY
why_this_matters: Acombamack preserves a Native placename for the Bellport area along Great South Bay, where records associate the name with a fishing place. Its many colonial-era spellings show how Indigenous geography entered English paperwork imperfectly, but still carried knowledge of water, foodways, and local movement. The South Shore was and remains more than a modern shoreline; it is part of Native coastal geography.
translation_content:
Recorded forms include Acombamack, Occombamack, Ockanbamack, Combamack, Accombomok, Accombomack, Occumbomock, Cumbamack, Owenamchock, and Owenamchog. Acombamack is interpreted as over against the fishing-place or on the other side of their fishing-place. Owenamchock is interpreted as beyond the fishing-place or the further fishing-place, with the exact relationship between these forms still uncertain.

Why Place Names Matter

“The study of place-names can reveal facts relating to the past and so yield information concerning the history, religion and civilization of the first occupants of the places concerned.”

— Augustine D. K. K. Ameka, The onomastics of principal Anlo town names (2018), PDF page 23
whereintheworld_content: The map placement near Bellport and Great South Bay for the Acombamack / Accombamack landscape is a general orientation point, not an exact deed-boundary or fishing-station coordinate.
